Repository Instructions

Source: AGENTS.md

This repository is an R package. When editing code, follow the existing package style closely rather than using generic R formatting defaults.

Synced Internal Helpers

Some internal helpers in R/internals.R are mirrored from package admisc. When editing code in this package, run the admisc sync check once per work session, using the environment variable:

DECLARED_CHECK_ADMISC_SYNC=true Rscript -e 'testthat::test_local(".", filter = "admisc-sync")'

The test does not mechanically sync or blindly compare entire function bodies. It verifies that all internal helper names which also exist in admisc are classified in tests/testthat/test-admisc-sync.R. If the check reports a new candidate, inspect the corresponding admisc implementation manually and then classify it as synced or intentionally package-specific.

R Code Style

  • Leave a space between a function name and its opening parenthesis, for example match.arg (...), inherits (...), length (...), and stop (...).
  • Leave a space between control-flow keywords and their opening parenthesis, for example if (...), for (...), and while (...).
  • Prefer the repository’s existing brace and else style:
    • opening braces stay on the same line as if, else, for, or function;
    • else generally starts on its own line after the preceding closing brace.
  • Use return (...) explicitly when returning final values from package functions, matching the surrounding code.
  • Keep S3 method names and exported functions consistent with nearby files. Backtick method names when the local style does so, especially for operators or dotted S3 methods.
  • Prefer local helper names and object names that fit the repository vocabulary. Do not introduce broad abstractions unless they clearly reduce duplicated package logic.
  • Keep edits focused. Avoid unrelated formatting churn, metadata updates, or refactors.

Tests

  • Add focused testthat coverage for behavior changes.
  • Prefer targeted checks first, for example: Rscript -e 'testthat::test_local(".", filter = "name")'.
  • If running R CMD check, note that unrelated package metadata issues may exist; do not change DESCRIPTION unless explicitly asked.
